label: verify-q2-literature

claims.claim: PDBbind-CASF leakage: ~600 similar pairs, 49% of CASF complexes
claims.source_says: nearly 600 such similarities were detected between PDBbind training and CASF complexes, involving 49% of all CASF complexes
claims.note: Read in the PMC full text (PMC12552120) of the Nature MI paper.

claims.claim: Label-lookup baseline gets CASF2016 Pearson 0.716 on PDBbind and 0.653 on CleanSplit
claims.source_says: Original PDBbind: (Pearson R = 0.716, r.m.s.e. = 1.517); CleanSplit: r.m.s.e. of 1.648 and a Pearson correlation of 0.653.
claims.note: Both numbers match; the baseline averages the labels of the five most similar training complexes.

claims.claim: Ligand-only and protein-only bias models match published ML scoring functions on CASF2016 (r 0.76/0.75 vs 0.74-0.82)
claims.source_says: LigandBias 0.76; ProteinBias 0.75; MLBSFs 0.74 (Pafnucy) to 0.82 (RFScore, SIGN, OnionNet-2). 'competitive in accuracy to these MLBSFs in almost all proposed benchmarks'
claims.note: Numbers from Table 1 of PMC11821266 match; I did not open the DOI itself.

claims.claim: Heterogeneous Ki noise floor: mean error 0.44 pKi, SD 0.54, max R2 0.81 (Kramer 2012); cross-assay IC50 Kendall tau 0.51 (Landrum 2024)
claims.source_says: Kramer: mean error of 0.44 pK(i) units, a standard deviation of 0.54, maximum possible R(2) 0.81. Landrum: with minimal curation Kendall's tau 'is only 0.51'.
claims.note: Read via Europe PMC abstracts; the 0.51 holds for minimal curation only (0.71 with maximal curation).

overall: All four key claims reproduce against the sources. Publisher pages gave 403/redirect, so I read the abstracts and full text through Europe PMC and PMC instead. One caveat: the Landrum 0.51 applies to minimal curation only.
